newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's assigns ratings to Bank of Asia.
newsitem.headline: Moody's assigns ratings to Bank of Asia.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it has assigned ratings of Baa2 and Prime-3 to Bank of Asia for its long- and short-term deposits, respectively.
Bank of Asia's senior debt was rated Baa2.
Moody's also assigned a Bank Financial Strength Rating (BFSR) of "D" to Bank of Asia.
Moody's said the ratings reflect Bank of Asia's improving trends in profitability, liquidity and capital as well as the bank's capable and professional management.
The ratings are constrained by Bank of Asia's modest domestic franchise, its relatively weak asset quality and its high dependence upon foreign funding, Moody's said.
Furthermore, the bank is facing an increasingly difficult macroeconomic environment as well as a more competitive market for financial services in the domestic Thai market.
The deposit ratings also incorporate the supportive regulatory environment created by the Bank of Thailand.
Moody's noted that Bank of Asia faces several important challenges over the medium-term.

Liquidity remains tight in the Thai banking system, it said. The onset of financial liberalization coupled with a relatively rigid foreign exchange rate system have triggered a massive inflow of short-term funding seeking higher yields in Thailand.

Moody's said that it appears that both Thai and foreign banks, including BIBFs (Bangkok International Banking Facilities) have borrowed relatively cheap foreign currency-denominated funds to on-lend at higher spreads to Thai domestic borrowers.

Moody's said that Thailand's increased exposure to short-dated funding has heightened the risk of potential liquidity strains over the short- to medium-term in the event that creditor sentiment deteriorates, possible leading to a sharp reversal or curtailment of such inflows.

Furthermore, the rating agency said, Thailand's financial markets are undergoing significant changes, including deregulation, increasing competititon from domestic and foreign financial entities and profitability pressures, which are more strongly felt by the smaller banks in the system.
Bank of Asia is the 11th largest bank in Thailand, with consolidated assets of 122 billion baht (approximately US$5 billion)n as of June 30, 1996, Moody's said.
